اسلام آباد: 14 مئی، 2026 وزیراعظم محمد شہباز شریف نے ہاؤسنگ کے شعبے میں اصلاحات کے حوالے سے جائزہ اجلاس کی صدارت کی. اجلاس سے گفتگو کرتے ہوئے وزیرِ اعظم نے کہا کہ بڑھتی ہوئی آبادی کے پیش نظر ہاؤسنگ کے شعبے میں اصلاحات وقت کی اہم ضرورت ہے. کم آمدنی والے طبقے کے لیے رہائش کی فراہمی، سستے گھروں کے منصوبے بشمول نجی شعبے کی حوصلہ افزائی اور عوامی سہولیات کی بہتری ہماری ترجیحات میں شامل ہیں. بڑھتی ہوئی آبادی اور بے ہنگم شہری پھیلاو کی وجہ سے زرعی زمین پر دباو بڑھ رہا ہے، جس کے لئے مناسب حکمت عملی کی ضرورت ہے۔ وزیرِ اعظم نے مزید کہا کہ ہاؤسنگ کے شعبے میں تمام معاملات کو ڈیجیٹائز اور آٹو میٹ کیا جائے گا تاکہ شفافیت کو فروغ ملے۔ ہاوسنگ سیکٹر میں بیرون ملک سرمایہ کاروں کو راغب کرنے کے لئے، اس سیکٹر کو ضابطہ کار کے تحت لانا ضروری ہے۔ اجلاس کو ہاؤسنگ سیکٹر میں اصلاحات کے حوالےسے تجاویز پیش کی گئیں. اجلاس کو بریفنگ میں بتایا گیا کہ ہاؤسنگ کے شعبے میں شفافیت لانے کے حوالے سے معتبر سرمایہ کاروں اور ڈویلپرز کو سہولیات کی فراہمی کے حوالے سے ریگیولیٹری فریم ورک سہل کیا جائے گا. ہاوسنگ اور ڈیولپمنٹ سیکٹر میں کام کرنے والوں کے لئے ایس ای سی پی، میں رجسٹریشن لازمی قرار دی جانی چاہئے۔ اجلاس کو مزید بتایا گیا کہ شہروں کے بے ترتیب پھیلاؤ کو روکنے کے حوالے سے بھی حکمت عملی بنائی جائے گی. بڑے شہروں میں اونچی عمارتوں اور ورٹیکل ایکسپینشن کی حوصلہ افزائی کی جائے گی. اجلاس کو بڑے شہروں کے لئے ماسٹر ٹاؤن پلاننگ کی تجویز بھی دی گئی. ڈویلپرز، خریداروں اور دیگر اسٹیک ہولڈرز کے حقوق کی تحفظ کے حوالےسے ون ونڈو سسٹم قائم کیا جانا چاہئیے. وزیراعظم نے ان تجاویز کے حوالےسے صوبوں کے ساتھ مشاورت کی ہدایت کی. اجلاس میں وفاقی وزیر اقتصادی امور احد خان چیمہ ، وفاقی وزیر ہاؤسنگ اینڈ ورکس میاں ریاض حسین پیر زادہ ، وفاقی وزیر داخلہ و انسداد منشیات محسن نقوی ، وفاقی وزیر قانون و انصاف اعظم نذیر تارڑ ، وزیراعظم کے مشیر برائے بین الصوبائی روابط رانا ثناء اللہ ، وزیر مملکت داخلہ طلال چوہدری ، وزیر مملکت برائے خزانہ و ریلوے بلال اظہر کیانی ، چئیرمین نیب لیفٹننٹ جنرل (ریٹائرڈ) نذیر احمد بٹ، اٹارنی جنرل منصور اعوان اور متعلقہ اعلیٰ سرکاری افسران نے شرکت کی۔ Video

Close to 100.6 million married Indian women aged 25–49 are outside the workforce. 85% who dropped out cited care-related reasons. In the latest #EPWD blog, Shravani Prakash, Cledwyn Fernandez, and Anjhana Ramesh unpack how the “motherhood penalty” in India extends far beyond individual careers to become a structural economic challenge. Drawing on data from the PLFS and Time Use Survey, the piece highlights how childcare responsibilities, unpaid care work, and unequal workplace structures continue to push millions of women out of the workforce during their prime working years. Data reveals: → Married women's workforce participation is 50% below the female average; married men's is 98%. → Single salaried women earn ~30% more than married salaried women. → Graduates make up the largest share of women exiting for childcare → India is losing its most educated women to an invisible care economy. → ₹52,600 crore is the conservative annual wage loss from this exit alone. → Women spend 341 minutes a day on unpaid care work — 8x more than men. → The ILO estimates redistributing care work could add $250 billion to India's GDP. From childcare infrastructure and shared parental leave to flexible work and care-friendly cities, the piece outlines why addressing care work must become central to economic policymaking rather than remain a private burden borne by women alone. Countries that have closed this gap stopped treating care as a private, feminine issue and started treating it as shared economic infrastructure. India has the evidence. The ecosystem is the next build. epwd-icrier.in/blog/labour-a…

மக்கள் கோபமடைந்துள்ளது வரி செலுத்துவது குறித்து அல்ல; தங்களுக்கு இழைக்கப்படும் அநீதி குறித்தே அவர்கள் கோபமடைந்துள்ளனர். பரிந்துரைக்கப்பட்டுள்ள இந்த 185A பிரிவு, வரி அறிக்கைகளை தாக்கல் செய்வதில் ஏற்படும் தாமதம் அல்லது பதிவு செய்வதில் ஏற்படும் தாமதம் போன்ற நிர்வாக ரீதியான தவறுகளைக் கூட குற்றச் செயல்களாக மாற்றுகிறது. இதன் பொருள் என்னவென்றால், வாழ்வாதாரத்திற்காக போராடும் ஒரு சிறு தொழில்முயற்சியாளரும், வேண்டுமென்றே பல மில்லியன் கணக்கில் வரி செலுத்துவதிலிருந்தும் தவிர்த்துக் கொள்ளுபவரும் சமமாகவே கருதப்பட முடியும் என்பதாகும். இது முற்றிலும் குறைபாடுள்ள ஒரு நிலைமையாகும். வரி முறையைச் சரிசெய்தல், உள்நாட்டு இறைவரித் திணைக்களத்தை (IRD) நவீனமயமாக்கல் மற்றும் வரி இணக்கத்தை எளிதாக்குவதற்குப் பதிலாக, சாதாரண மக்களைக் குற்றவாளிகளாக்கும் குறுக்கு வழியையே அரசாங்கம் பின்பற்றுகிறது. இவ்வளவு வேகமாக சட்டங்களை நிறைவேற்ற அவர்களுக்கு பலம் இருக்குமானால், உண்மையான ஊழல் எதிர்ப்புச் சட்டங்களுக்கு என்ன நடந்தது? நிதி மோசடி, பணச்சலவை மற்றும் பொதுச் சொத்துக்களைத் திருடியவர்களுக்கு எதிராக எடுக்கப்படும் நடவடிக்கைகளுக்கு என்ன நடந்தது? ஊழல்வாதிகளைத் தேடிச் செல்லுங்கள். உண்மையான மோசடி செய்பவர்களைக் கடுமையாகத் தண்டியுங்கள். ஆனால், சாதாரண மக்களுக்கு எதிராகச் சட்டத்தை ஒரு ஆயுதமாகப் பயன்படுத்தாதீர்கள். சட்டங்கள் மூலம் நீதி, விகிதாசாரத் தன்மை மற்றும் மக்களின் அரசியலமைப்பு ரீதியான உரிமைகள் மீறப்படும் சந்தர்ப்பங்களில் நாம் ஒருபோதும் மௌனமாக இருக்கமாட்டோம்.

ජනතාව කෝපයට පත්ව ඇත්තේ බදු ගෙවීම පිළිබඳව නොවේ. ඔවුන් කෝපයට පත්ව ඇත්තේ තමාට අසාධාරණ ලෙස සැලකීම පිළිබඳවයි. යෝජිත මෙම 185අ වගන්තිය මඟින්, බදු වාර්තා ගොනු කිරීම ප්‍රමාද වීම හෝ ලියාපදිංචි වීමේ ප්‍රමාදයන් වැනි පරිපාලනමය වැරදි පවා අපරාධ වරදවල් බවට පත් කරනු ලබයි. එහි අර්ථය නම්, ජීවත් වීමට වෙහෙසෙන සුළු පරිමාණ ව්‍යාපාරිකයෙකුට ද, හිතාමතා රුපියල් මිලියන ගණනින් බදු ගෙවීම් පැහැර හරින අයෙකුට හා සමානව සැලකිය හැකිය යන්නයි. එය දෝෂ සහගත තත්ත්වයකි. බදු ක්‍රමය නිවැරදි කිරීම, දේශීය ආදායම් දෙපාර්තමේන්තුව (IRD) නවීකරණය කිරීම සහ බදු අනුකූලතාවය පහසු කිරීම වෙනුවට, රජය කරන්නේ සාමාන්‍ය ජනතාව අපරාධකරුවන් කිරීම නමැති කෙටි මාවතට පිවිසීමයි. මෙතරම් වේගයෙන් නීති සම්මත කිරීමට ඔවුන්ට ශක්තියක් තිබේ නම්, සැබෑ දූෂණ විරෝධී පනත්වලට සිදුවූයේ කුමක්ද? මූල්‍ය වංචා, මුදල් විශුද්ධිකරණය සහ මහජන දේපළ සොරකම් කළ අයට එරෙහිව ගනු ලබන පියවරයනට සිදුවූයේ කුමක්ද? දූෂිතයන් හඹා යන්න. සැබෑ වංචාකාරයන්ට දැඩි ලෙස දඬුවම් කරන්න. එනමුත් සාමාන්‍ය ජනතාවට එරෙහිව අවියක් ලෙස නීතිය භාවිතා නොකරන්න. නීති මඟින් සාධාරණත්වය, සමානුපාතිකත්වය සහ ජනතාවගේ ආණ්ඩුක්‍රම ව්‍යවස්ථාපිත අයිතිවාසිකම් උල්ලංඝනය වන අවස්ථාවන්හි අපි කිසිසේත්ම නිහඬව නොසිටින්නෙමු.

People are not angry about paying taxes. People are angry about being treated unfairly. This proposed 185A clause turns even administrative mistakes like delays in filing returns or registration into criminal offences. That means a small businessman struggling to survive can be treated the same way as someone deliberately hiding millions in taxes. That is wrong. Instead of fixing the tax system, modernising the IRD, and making compliance easier, the Government is taking the shortcut of criminalising ordinary people. If they have the strength to pass laws this fast, then where are the real anti-corruption laws? Where is the action against financial fraud, money laundering, and those who stole public wealth? Go after the corrupt. Punish real fraudsters hard. But do not weaponise the law against the common man. We will never stay silent when laws go against fairness, proportionality, and the constitutional rights of the people.

I arrived in Kigali this afternoon from Nairobi, where we joined other African leaders at the Africa Forward Summit co-hosted by President Ruto and President Macron to advance a new model of partnership built on trade, investment, innovation, infrastructure, and shared prosperity. I thank my brother, President Paul Kagame, for the warm reception upon my arrival in Kigali and for our productive bilateral engagement at the Urugwiro presidential village. Nigeria and Rwanda understand what this moment requires. Africa must trade more with itself, move goods faster, connect its markets better, and give its entrepreneurs the continental scale they need to compete. Our discussions focused on expanding bilateral trade between our two countries. We are also in the early stages of discussions with RwandAir on a practical flat rate arrangement that can help Nigerian businesses ship their goods more predictably across the continent. As champions of the AfCFTA, Nigeria and Rwanda will continue to work together to deepen digital trade, strengthen market access, and remove the barriers that limit African enterprise. Furthermore, Nigeria is proud to host the AfCFTA Council of Ministers and Digital Trade Forum in June. We also look forward to welcoming the continent and the world for IATF and CANEX from November 5 to 11, 2026, and again in November 2027. From the Africa Forward Summit in Nairobi to the Africa CEO Forum in Kigali, my message remains the same. Africa’s future will not be built by speeches alone. It will be built by trade, investment, innovation, and the courage to trust one another’s markets. This is the path to shared and sustainable prosperity for our people and the continent. Nestled along the eastern coastline of India, Odisha is a land where spirituality, heritage, and nature come together in a deeply rooted cultural landscape. From ancient temples to vibrant festivals, the state reflects a timeless connection between devotion and everyday life. Home to iconic landmarks such as the Konark Sun Temple and the sacred Jagannath Temple in Puri, Odisha’s spiritual essence is brought to life through grand celebrations like the Rath Yatra and Durga Puja. Its rich traditions extend to classical dance forms, intricate handicrafts like Pattachitra and silver filigree, and diverse tribal communities that preserve age-old ways of life. Beyond its cultural depth, Odisha offers serene coastal experiences and ecological richness—from the tranquil shores of Puri to the vast expanse of Chilika Lake, a haven for migratory birds and unique biodiversity. Its cuisine, with dishes like Pakhala Bhata, Dalma, Chhena Poda, and Dahi Vada Aloo Dum, reflects a blend of simplicity and tradition rooted in local life. Whether it is exploring heritage sites, witnessing living traditions, or experiencing its natural beauty, Odisha offers a journey that is both enriching and enduring. Through a state-wise journey, it brings together India’s rich traditions, iconic landscapes, vibrant festivals, and living heritage, offering a holistic narrative of the nation’s unity in diversity. #DidYouKnow Aurangabad district in Bihar demonstrated how plastic waste can be effectively managed through Plastic Waste Management Units (PWMUs) under the Swachh Bharat Mission-Gramin. Between March 2023 and December 2024, the initiative converted non-biodegradable plastic waste into durable bricks through a process of cleaning, shredding, heating, and mixing with sand, reducing landfill burden and environmental pollution. Each unit processed 80-100 kg of plastic waste per day, producing 40-50 bricks, while promoting recycling, lowering carbon footprint, and supporting local livelihoods. The model highlighted the potential of circular economy approaches by turning waste into value-added construction materials. Such initiatives have been documented on the NITI for States (NFS) Knowledge Portal - an initiative under the State Support Mission. President Xi Jinping held talks with U.S. President Donald J. Trump. President Xi noted that transformation not seen in a century is accelerating across the globe, and the international situation is fluid and turbulent. The world has come to another crossroads. Can China and the United States overcome the Thucydides Trap and create a new paradigm of major-country relations? Can we meet global challenges together and provide greater stability for the world? Can we build a bright future together for our bilateral relations in the interest of the well-being of the two peoples and the future of humanity? These are the questions vital to history, to the world, and to the people. They are the questions of our times that the leaders of major countries need to answer together. President Xi stressed that the two countries have more common interests than differences, success in one is an opportunity for the other, and a stable bilateral relationship is good for the world. We should be partners, not rivals. We should help each other succeed and prosper together, and find the right way for major countries to get along well with each other in the new era. I look forward to our discussions on major issues important to our two countries and the world, and working together with you to set the course and steer the giant ship of China-U.S. relations, so as to make 2026 a historic, landmark year that opens up a new chapter in China-U.S. relations.

Gaza’s exceptionalism? There is a strange and recurring theme that treats Palestinians in Gaza as exempt from the basic realities of modern war. It suggests Gazans should remain exactly where they are, face no disruption, and expect reconstruction to simply restore the pre-October 7 reality, as if the devastation, the tens of thousands killed, and the political collapse should carry no structural consequences. This view ignores how every major conflict from Iraq and Syria to Yemen, Sudan, Libya, Ethiopia, Lebanon, Afghanistan, and Ukraine involved mass displacement and population relocation for their safety and security, shifts in governance, the removal of armed groups, and major political restructuring. Gaza is the only case where displacement has been entirely internal, leaving civilians with almost no safe alternatives and facing unbearable hardships and challenges, caught in between Israeli bombardment and Hamas’s control. The exceptionalism narrative insists that everything in Gaza must be smooth and consequence‑free: aid should flow flawlessly; civilians should never be asked to temporarily relocate; all needs must be met while everyone stays put; reconstruction should be guaranteed without any commitment to a new political or social contract; and Gaza should receive unlimited aid while its leaders retain the freedom to launch wars, provoke neighbors, and reject peace under the banner of “resistance.” A second pillar of this exceptionalism point of view is the belief that Hamas, the actor that triggered this disaster, is entitled to a say in the next steps and deserves to remain politically intact and recycled into yet another reconstruction phase, as has happened for two decades. Whether out of romanticization of “resistance” or avoidance of hard choices, this view demands rebuilding Gaza while its captors stay in place. But the international community and donor states will not fund a future where Gaza is expected to thrive while still held by jihadist adventurism and nihilistic governance. There is no perfect humanitarian delivery system, no perfect reconstruction with everyone staying put, and no scenario where Hamas is confronted while the population remains entirely stationary. Two decades of jihadism marketed as “resistance” have created consequences that can no longer be deferred. If Gaza is to be rebuilt and reborn, difficult decisions are unavoidable. The alternative is the status quo: a slow drip of aid that leaves two million people trapped in rubble, sewage, and despair. Creating genuinely safe zones outside of the “Yellow Line,” secured by an International Stabilization Force, is essential to moving civilians out of Hamas’s grip, shielding them from renewed Israeli attacks, and enabling the eventual rebuilding of Gaza.

A ten-year-old boy walked into a computer store in Recife, Brazil, and politely asked if he could use one of the tablets on display. The salesperson agreed and handed it to him. Instead of playing, the boy sat down and began working seriously. Store employees noticed he had taken out a notebook and pen, carefully writing down information from the screen. Curious, they asked him what he was doing. He explained that he had a geography assignment to complete, but his family didn’t own a computer and couldn’t afford one. The tablet was his only way to study. The moment, captured by the store’s security camera, quickly spread across social media. When the store owner learned the boy’s story, he decided to provide him with the equipment he needed to study and access the internet. The world isn’t fair. Some are born into comfort and opportunity, while others face constant limitation — not because of a lack of effort or ability, but because of inequality. #الشراكة_السعودية_الباكستانية تتجاوز الأطر التقليدية إلى "التحالف المتكامل ". وفق ركائز تؤكد أن الأمن والاقتصاد وجهان متوازيان: ​1. الصناعات الدفاعية: من الاستيراد إلى التصنيع المشترك ف​لم تعد العلاقة العسكرية تقتصر على التدريبات والتعاون الاستخباراتي، بل اتجهت نحو توطين الصناعات العسكرية. باكستان تمتلك خبرة عريقة في تصنيع المعدات الدفاعية، وهذا يتقاطع مباشرة مع مستهدفات رؤية 2030 لتوطين 50% من الإنفاق العسكري السعودي. ​القيمة المضافة: تبادل الخبرات التقنية في المجالات الدفاعية. ​2. الأمن الغذائي: الاستثمار في "سلة الغذاء" حيث ​تعتبر باكستان من أهم الوجهات ضمن استراتيجية المملكة للأمن الغذائي. ​فهناك توجه قوي للاستثمار في مساحات شاسعة من الأراضي الزراعية الباكستانية واستخدام تقنيات الري الحديثة لتأمين سلاسل إمداد مستقرة للمملكة، مما يحول القطاع الزراعي من نشاط تقليدي إلى قطاع استثماري مربح للجانبين. ​3. ممر الطاقة والبنية التحتية ف​باكستان تمثل حلقة وصل جغرافية تربط الشرق الأوسط بالصين وآسيا الوسطى. ​مشروع مصفاة النفط: الاستثمار السعودي في مصفاة تكرير عملاقة في ميناء "غوادر" ليس مجرد مشروع نفطي، بل هو تثبيت لموقع المملكة كلاعب رئيسي في تأمين احتياجات الطاقة لآسيا عبر ممرات أقصر وأكثر أماناً. ​4. التحول الرقمي والتكنولوجيا ​يمتلك قطاع التقنية في باكستان كوادر بشرية هائلة ومنافسة عالمياً. ​التكامل: يمكن للشركات السعودية الاستفادة من هذه الكوادر في مشاريع التحول الرقمي، بينما توفر المملكة البيئة الحاضنة والتمويل، مما يخلق "سوقاً تقنية" مشتركة قادرة على المنافسة. ​5. الاستقرار الأمني كضمانة للنمو ​يدرك البلدان أن أي تهديد لأمن الممرات المائية (مثل بحر العرب ومضيق هرمز) يؤثر مباشرة على أسعار الطاقة والتجارة العالمية. لذا، فإن التنسيق الأمني البحري والدفاعي المشترك هو الذي يوفر "المظلة الآمنة" التي تتدفق تحتها الاستثمارات بمليارات الدولارات. ​خلاصة القول: باكستان ليست مجرد "سوق"، بل هي شريك استراتيجي في سلاسل الإمداد (الطاقة، الغذاء، والدفاع). هذا التكامل هو ما يحول "الأمن المشترك" إلى ثروة مشتركة.

Not surprised by yet another NEET paper leak - it is only the latest in a long series of leaks and corruption issues in govt exams across India/our states. We have to stop pretending these are isolated failures of execution: they are the predictable output of an exam system that is brittle by design Sources of dysfunction: - Lowest-bid vendor selection (Eduquity at ₹171/candidate beating TCS at ₹311, despite being previously blacklisted) - Single-shot national exams where one glitch derails millions - Paper transport chains with compromised "last-mile" contractors - Rigid scheduling where one disruption triggers a national crisis - A coaching-industry-driven economy where families spend 5-8x their annual per-capita income on preparation International models show the way out: - SAT/GRE-style year-round, on-demand, computer-based testing - Multi-attempt models with best-score-counting - Stable, long-term vendor partnerships (France's Ministry-controlled vendors run for over a decade; the US uses AAMC/Prometric for 25+ years) - Military-grade logistics (South Korea's Suneung, China's Gaokao) This @swarajyamag report is the best you'll find explaining the systemic issue: swarajyamag.com/reports/brok…

The British Labor Party's energy policy is ensuring that Britain has no future in high-tech services as well as industry. Rolls-Royce will have to move to a more sensible country or go out of business. Nina Schick (@NinaDSchick) Britain now has the highest industrial electricity prices in the developed world. At 25p per kilowatt-hour, its power costs stand at double the EU average and quadruple those of the US (6p) and China (7p). But this isn’t just about the death of old industry. Just as cheap electricity determined the industrial powers of the past, it will now determine the AI superpowers of the future. The real competition is not about who builds the best AI models, but who can afford to run them. Sovereignty in this century is found in the physical ability to process Intelligence at an industrial scale. Britain’s current path is a dead end. There are 140 data centers in the UK’s grid connection queue, representing 50 GW of demand — more than the entire country’s current peak usage (45 GW). For many, the quoted connection date is 2040. As Intelligence proliferates, productivity will no longer be measured in man-hours, but in Tokens-per-Watt: how many units of ‘Intelligence’ a kilowatt-hour of electricity can buy. With its 25p rate, it is already 400% more expensive to buy Intelligence in Britain than in China or the US. This is a direct hit to the UK services sector, which accounts for 82% of the economy. As AI automates knowledge work, British firms must 'rent' intelligence from foreign clouds at predatory rates just to stay competitive. Even if Britain builds domestic AI infrastructure, the 25p barrier means it would be structurally uncompetitive from day one. This leaves only the path of outsourcing national productivity to foreign clouds, a permanent transfer of British wealth. True sovereignty requires a radical shift to dedicated, low-cost power for compute. Without cheap energy, Britain won’t just lose its factories — it may lose its offices, too. — http://nitter.perennialte.ch/NinaDSchick/status/2038964092954608105#m

До повномасштабного вторгнення бойовики терористичних проросійських угруповань контролювали приблизно 32% області. За перші 40 днів вторгнення через провал оборони на півдні України та оточення Маріуполя, кацап зумів захопити ще 22.4% Донеччини. Після цього темпи просування спали, адже Сили Оборони стали від Великої Новосілки до Вугледару, а кацап стирався у штурмах ДонУРу (Донецького укріпленого району). Історичний факт, що німецький Вермахт за неповні 47 місяців умудрився від Західного Бугу дійти до Москви та Сталінграду, а також повернутися в Берлін. 🚨 Ahead of Thursday’s resumption of Israel-Lebanon talks, I asked Israeli Ambassador to the U.S. Yechiel Leiter whether it’s accurate to say that discussions have moved past setting parameters for talks and could now be considered direct negotiations. “Almost accurate,” he said. “We've made some advancements over the initial meetings. Now we're going to move into, hopefully, setting the framework for two teams: One team that will deal with achieving peace, a peace treaty, full peace, as if Hezbollah doesn't exist, and a security track, as if the peace talks don't exist. We have to deal with security. We have to deal with disarming Hezbollah. This is the first time that the talks are not focused on when is the IDF going to withdraw? When is the IDF going to stop its kinetic activity in Lebanon? Everybody understands today that our presence in Lebanon is because Hezbollah is there, and Hezbollah is armed to the teeth, and Hezbollah is interested in firing missiles into our cities, towns, villages. We're not gonna let that happen anymore. So the focus is now on, number one, reaching a peace treaty, as if there's no Hezbollah, and fighting Hezbollah as if there's no peace treaty. And I think we're going to accomplish both. That's our position.“ Asked to compare that with the situation in Gaza, in which the Board of Peace is trying to move forward despite Hamas’ refusal to disarm, Leiter told me, “It’s important to understand we're not going to let the process stand still, but we're not going to be able to implement the peace that we signed unless the second track is fulfilled, and that's the dismantlement of Hezbollah. We cannot allow a situation any longer where, every few years, they decide at their will, at their discretion, when to shoot missiles. We have to go back in. We lose soldiers, G-d forbid, and we end up in a situation which is completely untenable. We have no immediate plans of withdrawal, and we have no designs in Lebanese territory at the same time, but we have designs on our security. We are going to operate for the security of our citizens, period, and that's something that the Lebanese government just has to understand.” Asked if he believes there is a true partner for long-term peace on the other side, Leiter told me, “I do. I think the majority of the Lebanese people - and we're even seeing this among the Shiites in Lebanon - the polls are showing, deep surveys of the population in Lebanon is showing, that the Shiites, which used to only support a peace agreement with Israel at five or 10%, has now moved to 40, 50% against Hezbollah. That's very significant. So we have to bring that to manifest itself. That's what we're working on. We have a lot of work cut out for us. This is not going to be an easy process, because there's 30-40, years of different tracks, of doing things differently, and the Lebanese are also very hesitant about moving forward, even though they want Hezbollah out as much as we do. But they have their internal politics. It's not exactly the most functional state, and we have to be patient, but be firm at the same time. We’re not going to let our guard down. We're not going to give up anything that is central to our security. That has to be perfectly clear. But I do think that the shared interest in freeing that country from Hezbollah is ultimately going to win the day and be vindicated.”

Courtesy Call on Chief of Army Staff by UN Resident Coordinator Dhaka, 13 May 2026 (Wednesday): H.E. Ms. Carol Flore-Smereczniak, United Nations Resident Coordinator in Bangladesh paid a courtesy call on General Waker-Uz-Zaman, SBP, OSP, SGP, psc Chief of Army Staff of Bangladesh Army at Army Headquarters today. The meeting marked the Ms. Carol Flore-Smereczniak’s first official interaction with the Chief of Army Staff after assuming her appointment on 23 March 2026. During the meeting, the UN Resident Coordinator highly appreciated the Bangladesh Army’s longstanding and significant contributions to United Nations Peacekeeping Operations and its unwavering commitment to global peace and stability, particularly during the current challenging period faced by UN peacekeeping missions worldwide. She expressed deep condolences for the peacekeepers who sacrificed their lives while serving under the UN flag, especially those who lost their lives in Abyei in December 2025. The UN Resident Coordinator also commended Bangladesh’s strong focus on the Women, Peace and Security (WPS) agenda through the deployment of a significant number of female peacekeepers in various UN missions. She further praised the Bangladesh Army’s role in maintaining internal security since July 2024. I arrived in Kigali this afternoon from Nairobi, where we joined other African leaders at the Africa Forward Summit co-hosted by President Ruto and President Macron to advance a new model of partnership built on trade, investment, innovation, infrastructure, and shared prosperity. I thank my brother, President Paul Kagame @PaulKagame, for the warm reception upon my arrival in Kigali and for our productive bilateral engagement at the Urugwiro presidential village. Nigeria and Rwanda understand what this moment requires. Africa must trade more with itself, move goods faster, connect its markets better, and give its entrepreneurs the continental scale they need to compete. Our discussions focused on expanding bilateral trade between our two countries. We are also in the early stages of discussions with RwandAir on a practical flat rate arrangement that can help Nigerian businesses ship their goods more predictably across the continent. As champions of the AfCFTA, Nigeria and Rwanda will continue to work together to deepen digital trade, strengthen market access, and remove the barriers that limit African enterprise. Furthermore, Nigeria is proud to host the AfCFTA Council of Ministers and Digital Trade Forum in June. We also look forward to welcoming the continent and the world for IATF and CANEX from November 5 to 11, 2026, and again in November 2027. From the Africa Forward Summit in Nairobi to the Africa CEO Forum @africaceoforum in Kigali, my message remains the same. Africa’s future will not be built by speeches alone. It will be built by trade, investment, innovation, and the courage to trust one another’s markets. This is the path to shared and sustainable prosperity for our people and the continent. Bola Ahmed Tinubu, GCFR

Here’s the good news: the United States is probably one of the safest countries on the planet when it comes to an Iran-driven energy crisis. America exports natural gas, coal, and refined fuels, which means geography and shale have combined to give the U.S. something most countries no longer have: energy insulation. The bigger issue is what happens next. Energy shocks no longer stay neatly contained, and if countries overseas start scrambling for fuel, prices of globally traded commodities spike right alongside them. Coal, industrial metals, shipping capacity, and electrical components all become more expensive and harder to source. That’s where the American grid could run into trouble. Not because we lack energy, but because we import a huge amount of the equipment needed to maintain and expand power infrastructure. Transformers already take more than a year to build, and a global supply crunch would make those delays significantly worse. #powergrid #energy #infrastructure #geopolitics

Counting on China looks like Trump's last arrow in the quiver to pressure Tehran—short of war, yet above diplomacy. But he's in trouble. Both Iran and China know that Trump is cornered and scrambling for a face-saving solution after a string of failures with Iran. So China won't give him what he wants unless he backs down in a way that serves Chinese interests—interests that, as it happens, align with those of Iran and the GCC states. Nor will China help him wriggle out of this crisis without offering a proper alternative in return. "Innocent passage" may become the password that lets Trump retreat gracefully—allowing him to climb down through direct coordination with China and indirect understanding with Iran. That would restore commercial navigation, free from the obstacles Washington imposed in the Strait of Hormuz for three weeks, which had blocked safe passage. This outcome wouldn't go against Iran's wishes. On the contrary, Iran would see it as a convenient vehicle to advance its own project for managing the strait—especially if it had already coordinated the matter with China before Trump's visit. Such a solution might be the only one compatible with Tehran's wartime gains, without requiring a direct agreement that lifts sanctions. Otherwise, for Tehran, going to war would be less costly than making concessions to its enemies. And China knows this very well.

#Hungary’s political transition presents the #EU with a narrow but critical window for strategic influence. In this new #ECFR commentary from @PiotrBuras1 and Pawel Zerka they outline six insights from a post-election Hungary. A new government under Peter Magyar is widely expected to shift Budapest closer to EU positions on Ukraine, Russia, and broader geopolitical alignment. But there are risks, if handled incorrectly. The core insight for decision-makers: Magyar’s mandate is primarily domestic. Hungarian voters are prioritising systemic reform at home over foreign policy realignment. This creates a sequencing challenge for the EU. The policy implication is not hesitation, but calibration. The EU should maintain conditionality and strategic pressure, while allowing political space for domestic consolidation. Supporting institutional reform and governance credibility in Hungary is not separate from geopolitical alignment. The question is no longer whether Hungary will change, but how the EU can calibrate and collaborate to ensure that change is both deep and lasting. भूमिपुत्रांच्या हक्कांसाठी लढणाऱ्या लोकनेत्याचा गौरव सोहळा मुख्यमंत्री देवेंद्र फडणवीस आणि केंद्रीय मंत्री नितीन गडकरी यांच्या प्रमुख उपस्थितीत आज उलवे, नवी मुंबई येथे लोकनेते रामशेठ ठाकूर यांचा अमृत महोत्सवी अभिष्टचिंतन सोहळा व 'रामशेठ ठाकूर पब्लिक स्कूल'चे उदघाटन व कोनशिला अनावरण पार पडले. मुख्यमंत्री देवेंद्र फडणवीस यावेळी म्हणाले, रामशेठ ठाकूर यांचा हा सत्कार केवळ एका व्यक्तीचा नसून, सामान्य माणसाने असामान्य कार्य कसे करावे याची प्रेरणा देणाऱ्या व्यक्तिमत्त्वाचा गौरव आहे. ठाकूर यांनी कर्मवीर भाऊराव पाटील यांच्या रयत शिक्षण संस्थेतून ‘कमवा आणि शिका’ योजनेतून शिक्षण पूर्ण केले आणि पुढे शिक्षक म्हणून काम करत समाजकार्यात स्वतःला झोकून दिले. स्वतःला शिक्षण घेताना आलेल्या अडचणी इतरांच्या वाट्याला येऊ नयेत, यासाठी त्यांनी आयुष्यभराची कमाई खर्च करून शिक्षण संस्था उभारून अनेक होतकरू विद्यार्थ्यांना शिक्षणाची संधी उपलब्ध करून दिली. रामशेठ ठाकूर यांचा संघर्षमय प्रवास थक्क करणारा आहे. साधी नोकरी करत असतानाही त्यांनी धाडसाने विविध कामे केली. स्थानिकांना न्याय मिळावा आणि रोजगाराच्या संधी उपलब्ध व्हाव्यात यासाठी त्यांनी मोठी आंदोलने उभी केली. स्वर्गीय दि. बा. पाटील यांच्या भूमिपुत्रांच्या हक्कांसाठीच्या आंदोलनातही त्यांनी महत्त्वाची भूमिका बजावली असे प्रतिपादन मुख्यमंत्री फडणवीस यांनी केले. लोकसभेपर्यंतचा राजकीय प्रवास केल्यानंतर त्यांनी सक्रीय राजकारणातून बाजूला होत समाजकार्यासाठी स्वतःला समर्पित केले. रायगड आणि नवी मुंबई परिसराच्या विकासात त्यांचे योगदान भविष्यात सुवर्णाक्षरांनी लिहिले जाईल, असेही मुख्यमंत्री फडणवीस यांनी नमूद केले. यावेळी मंत्री गणेश नाईक, मंत्री ॲड. आशिष शेलार, मंत्री आदिती तटकरे, मंत्री भरत गोगावले, खासदार सुनील तटकरे, खासदार श्रीरंग आप्पा बारणे, आमदार रविंद्र चव्हाण, आमदार प्रशांत ठाकूर व इतर मान्यवर उपस्थित होते. @Dev_Fadnavis @nitin_gadkari @NaikSpeaks @ShelarAshish @iAditiTatkare @ibharatgogawale @SunilTatkare @MPShrirangBarne @RaviDadaChavan @ithakurprashant #Maharashtra #DevendraFadnavis #AmritMahotsav
